Una fracción es una división sin termina: A fraction is an unfinished division. This topic finishes it: dividing produces decimals, and it turns out they can only come out in three ways. Then the road back is travelled, from decimal to fraction, and you learn to say how much is lost by rounding.
Un número decimal es lo que se obtiene a: A decimal number is what you get by extending place value to the right: after the units come the tenths, the hundredths, the thousandths… each place is worth ten times less than the one before.
La coma no es una frontera entre dos núm: The decimal point is not a border between two numbers: it is just the mark showing where the units are. That is why the rules for operating are the same as with whole numbers, with the single precaution of lining the points up properly.
Los decimales tal y como los usamos los: Decimals as we use them were popularised by Simon Stevin in 1585 with a pamphlet titled De Thiende (“The tenth”), in which he argued that with them anybody could do a merchant's sums “without fractions”. Curiously he proposed writing 3.47 as 3⓪4①7②. The decimal comma took hold soon after in much of Europe; the point is the English convention, and that is why calculators and programs use it.
Al dividir dos enteros solo pueden pasar: When you divide two whole numbers only three things can happen, and only three:
el denominador irreducible solo tiene fa: the denominator in lowest terms has only factors 2 and 5
el denominador tiene 2 o 5 <em>y</em> al: the denominator has 2 or 5 and some other factor
La división de dos enteros <strong>nunca: Dividing two whole numbers never gives an infinite non-recurring decimal. The possible remainders are finite in number, so sooner or later one repeats and from then on everything repeats. Numbers with infinite decimals and no period do exist —$\pi$, $\sqrt{2}$— but they do not come from any fraction: they are the irrationals.
La división que se muerde la cola: The division that bites its own tail
Elige una fracción y mira los restos que: Choose a fraction and watch the remainders come out. As soon as a remainder repeats, the period is closed.
Al dividir entre 7 solo hay 6 restos pos: Dividing by 7 there are only 6 possible non-zero remainders. How many digits at most can the period of $\frac{1}{7}$ have? Commit before pressing.
Que $1/3$ sea periódico en base 10 depen: That $1/3$ recurs in base 10 depends on the base, and this has an everyday consequence: in base 2, the computer's base, $0{.}1$ recurs. That is why in almost any programming language $0{.}1 + 0{.}2$ does not give exactly $0{.}3$. It is not a fault in the computer: it is the same phenomenon that stops $1/3$ from being written with terminating decimals. The solution banking uses is not to store euros with decimals, but to count in whole cents.
El desarrollo binario de $0{,}1$ se pued: The binary expansion of $0{.}1$ can be looked at digit by digit in [[maq-bits|the topic on bits]], next to those of $1/4$ or $5/8$, which do end. The rule is the same as here, with 2 in the role that 2 and 5 have here: only fractions whose denominator is a power of two terminate.
De decimal a fracción: la fracción gener: From decimal to fraction: the generating fraction
Todo decimal exacto o periódico se puede: Every terminating or recurring decimal can be turned into a fraction. The trick is always the same: multiply by powers of 10 so that the infinite decimal parts line up, and subtract.
Merece la pena ver de dónde sale la del: It is worth seeing where the pure recurring one comes from, because it is a lovely piece of reasoning. Let $x = 0{.}\overline{36}$. Then $100x = 36{.}\overline{36}$. Subtracting, the infinite tails cancel: $99x = 36$, so $x = \frac{36}{99}$.
La generatriz de un periódico mixto, des: The generating fraction of a mixed recurring decimal, from scratch
Escribir $x = 0{,}2\\overline{3} = 0{,}2: Write $x = 0{.}2\overline{3} = 0{.}2333\ldots$ as a fraction, without using the memorised rule.
Primero se aparta el anteperiodo multipl: First the non-recurring part is moved aside by multiplying by 10: $10x = 2{.}\overline{3} = 2{.}333\ldots$ Now the infinite tail starts right after the point.
El 2 no se repite. ¿Por cuánto hay que m: The 2 does not repeat. What do you have to multiply by so that what is left after the point is only the period?
Se multiplica otra vez por 10, una posic: You multiply by 10 again, one place for each digit of the period: $100x = 23{.}\overline{3} = 23{.}333\ldots$
¿Cuánto hay que desplazar la coma para q: How far do you have to shift the point so that the two infinite tails line up?
Se restan las dos: $100x - 10x = 23{,}33: You subtract the two: $100x - 10x = 23{.}333\ldots - 2{.}333\ldots$. The tails are identical and cancel: $90x = 21$.

La regla «periodo con anteperiodo, menos: The rule “period with the non-recurring part, minus the non-recurring part, over nines and zeros” is exactly this calculation: $\frac{23 - 2}{90}$. If you understand where it comes from, there is no need to memorise it.
De ahí sale el famoso $0{,}\\overline{9}: From this comes the famous $0{.}\overline{9} = 1$. If $x = 0{.}\overline{9}$, then $10x = 9{.}\overline{9}$ and subtracting gives $9x = 9$, that is, $x = 1$. It is not an approximation nor a trick: they are two ways of writing the same number.

Equivocarse en 1 cm midiendo un lápiz es: Being 1 cm out measuring a pencil is a disaster; being 1 cm out measuring a football pitch makes no difference. The absolute error is the same; the relative one is not. That is why the relative one is the one that really informs, and it is usually given as a percentage.

Su generatriz es $\\frac{9}{9} = 1$. Son: Its generating fraction is $\frac{9}{9} = 1$. They are the same number written two ways, just like $\frac{1}{2}$ and $0{.}5$.
El error relativo es lo que decide si un: The relative error is what decides whether a measurement is any use. Being a centimetre out measuring a room is irrelevant; the same centimetre on an engine part turns it into scrap. That is why industrial drawings do not give a measurement but a tolerance —$40{.}00 \pm 0{.}05$ mm— and why a clinical test result always comes with its margin: a value without its error is not a datum, it is an impression.
